title: Capoeira
description: Capoeira is an Afro-Brazilian cultural art that incorporates martial arts, dance, singing, and music. To include movement.

title: Art, Sport, and Culture in Contemporary Brazil
description: Brazilian culture and history to include capoeira, carnaval, forro, funk, ju-jitsu, samba, soccer, street art, and street theatre. Ethnic and racial diversity, nationalism, regional identity, right to urban space, rural and urban life.

title: Latin American Documentary Practices
description: Introduction to Latin American documentary film and photography. Aesthetics, film movements, and manifestos; memory and storytelling to contemporary times. Close reading and analysis of visual culture.

title: Literature and Film of Black Brazil
description: Afro-Brazilian prose, poetry, non-fiction writing and cinema. Race and cultural resistance in Brazil.

title: Brazilian Democracy and Society
description: Interdisciplinary examination of Brazilian democracy from the republic to today. To include topics of authoritarianism, democratic transition, LGBTQIA+ rights, environmental movement, economic policy, the reactionary turn and Black feminist resistance. Materials include ethnography, historiography, memoirs, documentary film, and digital media.

title: The Amazon is the Center of the World
description: Amazonia as a transnational region. Cosmovisions and narratives from the Amazon. Film, literature, and visual art. Indigenous rights and environmental activism,  sustainable development. Amazonia in the Latin American imaginary.

title: Creative Interventions in South American Streets: Activism, Art, and the City
description: Dynamics, history, and movements of public art and street art. Flash mobs, graffiti, memorials, muralism, pixação, and other art in public space. Political and social implications of art including commodification, gentrification, and policy. Includes stencil workshop and creative final project. No artistic experience required.

title: Brazilian Studies Capstone Seminar
description: Culminating learning experience of Brazilian studies major. Brazilian studies and contemporary Brazilianist scholarship. Preparation of 20-page capstone paper.

title: Sport in Brazilian Society
description: Brazilian jiu-jitsu, capoeira, soccer, and surfing. Intersections of gender, politics, race, and sport to include film, literature, and scholarship from social sciences.

title: Experimental Topics
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree.
